issue: The gated job 20260903-fix-claude-model-requests-failin-42986cfa ended "EXHAUSTED: graph exhausted maxCostUsd 5 at 7.69" at superstep 3 with `implement` never started (checkpoint-000004.json: status "exhausted", nodes.implement.status "exhausted", runs 0). `/kpi <job>` cannot revive it: GraphEngine.restore keeps it exhausted because the cost still exceeds the cap (engine.ts L680-682) and resumeLoop then throws "Cannot resume graph in exhausted state" (gated-loop.ts L1727-1729). More generally the engine ends runs on its own initiative from counters and clocks (maxCostUsd, timeoutMs, maxSteps, maxNodeRuns, maxRounds, maxTransientRetries) and from repeated-output detection, contradicting the owner's decision that graphs never fail: transient failures must retry indefinitely with visible backoff, no-progress must re-plan, and the only stop is the operator.
root_cause: Run termination is designed as a budget: packages/coding-agent/src/kpi/extensions/graph/budget.ts L102-125 (findExhaustedRunLimit: maxSteps, timeoutMs, maxCostUsd) and L135-149 (findExhaustedNodeLimit: maxRounds/maxNodeRuns) are consulted by engine.ts L1261-1264, L1274-1279 and L1307-1322 and turn into `exhaust()` (engine.ts L1191-1209, status "exhausted", one loop.terminal EXHAUSTED); transient retries are capped at MAX_TRANSIENT_RETRIES=2 (stop.ts L6, engine.ts L1144-1146, L1363-1366); the stop reducer turns a repeated fingerprint/failing-AC set into NO_PROGRESS and `round >= maxRounds` into EXHAUSTED (stop.ts L299-306) which the driver returns as a terminal (gated-loop.ts L1489-1516); and every such status is a product terminal in run-store.ts L391 so the job is no longer live or resumable. The fixture was killed by the maxCostUsd branch (budget.ts L118-123) with cost 7.69 against the graph default 5 (coding-loop.gated.json L403-409).

docs.what: Retitle 'US-05 — Self-healing loop and the operator stop'. Story: 'As an operator, I need the loop to keep delivering my intent — retrying, re-planning — and to wait for me rather than end on its own; only I stop it.' ACs: AC-05.1 Run states are exactly RUNNING, NEEDS_HUMAN, DONE, STOPPED; only DONE and STOPPED are finished, NEEDS_HUMAN carries a recovery reason and is resumable with /kpi <job>. AC-05.2 The same output_fingerprint or the same failing AC set twice routes back to plan with plan.repair (round, reason, failing_ac, evidence_ref) as feedback. AC-05.3 Rounds are unbounded; a repeat after a re-plan pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (no_progress) offering Give guidance / Keep going / Stop in the TUI and the resume command unattended. AC-05.4 Write outside write_allow pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (bounds) without a commit. AC-05.5 Untestable reviewer issue pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (review). AC-05.6 A transient 429 retry is not a new round; a provider refusal that cannot fail over pauses NEEDS_HUMAN (provider) with the real reason and the resume command. AC-05.7 Transient failures (http 408/429/5xx, timeout, transport) retry for as long as it takes with 1s doubling backoff capped at 60s, one node.retry event and one notification per retry, checkpoint before each wait. AC-05.8 No spend cap, clock, step, node-run or round counter ends a run; cost and elapsed time are reported only; a checkpoint written under a retired cap resumes. Update AC-02.7 (L114) to 'ROUND n'. Traceability table row US-05 unchanged pointer.
Delete the --max-cost-usd / --timeout-ms / --max-rounds rows; `/kpi stop` row reads 'Abort the running loop, write STOPPED; resumable with /kpi <job>'.
Remove task.limits; add node.retry to the EVT type list and give loop.terminal the status set DONE | NEEDS_HUMAN | STOPPED plus recovery.

Replace the table with the four run states and a recovery table (bounds, review, no_progress, provider, delivery, research, stack, branch, contract, ship, ac_quality) stating for each what the operator does and that /kpi <job> resumes. Replace 'Default caps…' with 'No caps: cost and elapsed time are reported (state.json cost_usd, elapsed_ms) and never enforced.' Replace the retry line with 'Retry ≠ round. Transient http 408/429/5xx, timeout, transport: same round, unbounded retries, backoff 1s doubling to a 60s ceiling, node.retry event and notification each time, checkpoint before the wait; the per-request idle timeout (httpIdleTimeoutMs, default 300000) is what turns a hung provider into a timeout.' Add 'No progress: a repeated output fingerprint or failing AC set routes to plan with plan.repair; a repeat after a re-plan pauses NEEDS_HUMAN/no_progress.'

Node types `agent | set | human | pause`; conditional list: 'bounds.held == false → pause bounds (resume test)', 'review untestable → pause review (resume implement)', 'progress.repeated and re-plan tried → pause no_progress (resume plan)', 'progress.repeated → plan'; document the facts progress.repeated, plan.repair_tried, plan.repair.
Add: 'Paused runs re-arm at their resume targets on restore; the engine never ends a run from a counter or clock; retries are unbounded and checkpointed; /kpi stop aborts through an AbortSignal.'
Example line becomes `K-π  LOOP gated r2  STAGE implement  GATE human  AC 4/5`.

UAT-02: 'ROUND n'. UAT-05 retitled 'Self-healing loop and the operator stop'; question 'When it cannot succeed yet, does it keep trying and re-plan, and does it wait for me instead of dying?'; action: identical output twice; same failing AC set twice after a re-plan; fixtures/bounds-violation/; a reviewer issue with no test; a stub provider answering 429 then 503 then hanging; /kpi stop mid-backoff then /kpi <job>. Pass evidence: re-plan with repair.json, then NEEDS_HUMAN no_progress with the select; NEEDS_HUMAN bounds / review with resume; node.retry events with growing delays capped at 60s and no terminal; STOPPED then a resumed run; no other status vocabulary; the retried 429 did not increment the round. ACs AC-05.1–05.8.

risks: Removing every bound means a job can genuinely run forever unattended (provider down for a weekend, a plan that never converges): cost keeps accruing on metered pools and the only stop is /kpi stop; the board, node.retry events and the re-plan notifications are the only mitigation. The owner accepted this explicitly.

Treating a failed `test` round as a verifier event changes ROUND counting (implement↔test cycles now count); any existing gated-loop/autopilot test asserting a specific round after a red test run must be re-read; the alternative (bounding implement↔test only by review rounds) would leave that inner loop with no progress detection once maxNodeRuns/maxSteps are gone.

Edge exclusivity: route() (engine.ts L783-810) unions every firing edge, so the new test/review three-way splits must be exactly exclusive over progress.repeated × plan.repair_tried or a superstep will schedule implement and plan together (commitResults then fails on a shared path). The graph-routing test above pins it.

Legacy runs on disk (eight UNSAFE/EXHAUSTED state.json files in .kpi/runs) become live NEEDS_HUMAN jobs under the new isLiveJob; the newest of them will reappear on the board and own bare follow-ups (routing.ts L96/L134 refuses kpi_start_job while a job is live) until `/kpi stop` or a resume. This is the intended semantics but is a visible behaviour change for the operator.

`/kpi stop` now aborts in-process work: aborting a session mid-tool-call relies on GraphAgentSession.abort (core AgentSession.abort exists, L1641) and on the sleeper honouring the signal; if a node has already mutated the worktree the STOPPED checkpoint records the node as running and a resume continues that same run — documented, but the operator must know a resume reruns the interrupted node's prompt.

Facts are computed once per superstep for every active node, so `progress.repeated` is only meaningful on edges from test/review; if a future graph reads it from another node it will see a stale witness. The observe(active) guard plus the graph-routing test bound this.

A re-plan rewrites stack.json and clears task.current_module_id; freezeCurrentSlice (stack.ts L513-518) then re-freezes from the new stack. If the plan node fails schema validation after a re-plan the run pauses NEEDS_HUMAN/contract — acceptable, but the operator sees a contract pause rather than a no-progress one.

Event schema and metric-runs graders change vocabulary; any external tooling grepping loop.terminal for EXHAUSTED/UNSAFE breaks. The traceability map, pty rows and metric runs are updated here; nothing else in-repo reads those tokens.

Backoff ceiling 60s without jitter means many parallel nodes (maxConcurrency 2) retry in lockstep against a rate-limited provider; the accounts balancer's cooldown/failover (accounts/index.ts L639-685) is what spreads load, not the engine.
open_questions: Automatic re-plan budget: this design allows exactly one automatic re-plan per operator touch (plan.repair_tried = repairs >= 1, reset on Give guidance / Keep going / resume). Does the owner want a different count (e.g. two automatic re-plans before the pause)?

Should a failed `test` round count as a ROUND on the board (this design: yes, because it is one implement→verify cycle and the failing AC set is the witness), or should ROUND count only review verdicts as today?
Backoff: 1s doubling to a 60s ceiling with no jitter is the proposal; confirm the ceiling and that jitter is not wanted.

Should a NEEDS_HUMAN (paused) job own bare follow-ups and block kpi_start_job as a live job does today (routing.ts L96/L134), or should only RUNNING jobs own follow-ups while paused jobs merely stay on the board and resumable?
Should the operator's `/kpi stop` on a run that is mid-tool-call abort the provider request immediately (this design) or let the current node finish its prompt and stop at the next checkpoint?

Legacy runs: is mapping old UNSAFE/EXHAUSTED/NO_PROGRESS/BLOCKED state files to a live NEEDS_HUMAN acceptable, or should old runs stay finished unless explicitly resumed (which would require keeping a legacy-status read path)?
Should this land as a tracked remediation package (RP-20) in docs/remediation-plan.md, given AGENTS.md L3 names that file as the only active work queue, or is the PRD/spec/uat amendment sufficient?
Keeping the event name `loop.terminal` for a NEEDS_HUMAN pause (with a recovery field) avoids touching every reader; is a rename to a pause event wanted despite the extra churn?
